question.leadin: His death and that of his wife Sophie prompted the July Crisis.

question.clue: His wife was never permitted in the royal carriage, as a condition of his marriage to the lower-class woman after he became heir apparent following the death of his cousin Rudolf and father Charles Louis.

swap.text: A Congress in this Austrian city attempted to create a "balance of power" in Europe after Napoleon's defeat.
swap.clue: This city, the seat of the Hapsburg monarchy, served as a dual capital with Budapest after an 1867 compromise with Hungary.

question.leadin: Answer the following about some of the Revolutions of 1848.
question.text: The Revolutions of 1848 shattered the delicate Concert of Europe established by this Austrian statesman to restore the European balance of power at the Congress of Vienna, which this leader hosted.
question.clue: The Academic Legion forced this man's resignation during the Revolutions of 1848.

swap.text: This first Austro-Hungarian Kaiser und Koenig ruled for 68 years. The assassination of his heir Archduke Ferdinand led to his invasion of Serbia and the start of World War I.
swap.clue: This man's reign saw the provinces of Venetia and Lombardy ceded to Italy.

question.text: Name this Austrian queen whose inheritance was justified by her father Charles VI's Pragmatic Sanction. Her accession was disputed in the War of Austrian Succession.
question.clue: Wenzel Kaunitz accepted Zator and Auschwitz in the first partition of Poland as the advisor of this ruler.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Kingdom of Italy.
swap.text: The Kingdom of Italy fought against this nation and its ally Germany at the Battle of Caporetto which was a decisive victory for this nation. This nation used the acronym k.u.k to represent its dual monarchy.
swap.answerHtml: Austria-Hungary [or The Kingdoms and Lands Represented in the Imperial Council and the Lands of the Holy Hungarian Crown of St. Stephen; do not accept or prompt on “Austria” or “Hungary” or “Austrian Empire”]

question.leadin: Answer the following about self-identified enlightened despots.
question.text: When asked his thoughts on the American Revolution, this Austrian ruler and enlightened despot replied, "Madam, it is my trade to be a King". This son of Maria Theresa liberalized the curriculum of the University of Vienna and abolished the Robot Patent.
question.clue: This ruler sent generals Lacy and Laudon on a series of tactical maneuvers in one conflict that saw little actual fighting, the War of Bavarian Succession, and, in response to the peasants' revolt of Horea, abolished serfdom.

swap.text: This monarch initially refused to recognize Karl Lueger's election as mayor. Franz Ferdinand was the heir of this first and only Emperor of Austria-Hungary, a position which he held until his death in 1916.

question.text: This Austrian emperor created the Dual Monarchy with Hungary and reigned for over 60 years. Franz Ferdinand was the nephew and heir of this ruler until his assassination.
question.clue: This ruler. After the death of Felix of Schwarzenberg, Alexander Bach became the leading policymaker of his reign.

swap.text: Becoming the ruler of and following the Revolutions of 1848, he led his country into WWI before dying in 1916.
swap.answer: Franz-Josef I or Francis Joseph I

question.text: In Austria, the revolutions led to the resignation of this increasingly unpopular conservative chancellor, who called the Congress of Vienna and will be played by Bruce Arthur in an upcoming straight-to-DVD feature.
question.clue: He gained the trust of von Hardenberg at the Berlin Convention, and was able to obtain Belgium, Lombardy, and Venice.

question.text: This Chancellor capitalized on the "self-elimination" of parliament in 1933 to assume emergency powers and ban all parties except his Fatherland Front, kicking off the civil war between Austrofascists and Austromarxists.
